rulers.name: Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte
rulers.title: President of the Republic (elected 10 December 1848)
rulers.note: Infobox '1848-1852'; the page records the coup of the night of 1/2 December 1851 ('the anniversary of his uncle Napoleon's coronation in 1804') and the establishment of the Second Empire on 2 December 1852.

keyframe_review.note: 629,631 km2: France with the overseas outline Cliopatria also gives the Second Empire's 1853 shape (bbox -61.8 to 88.5 E, -21.4 to 51.2 N: the Antilles, Guiana, Reunion, French India). The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible. The page mentions the 'Colony of Algeria' only as a predecessor entry and gives no 1848 annexation, so Algeria, drawn by the french-algeria row, is not part of this shape.

629,765 km2 for 1849-1852, 134 km2 over 1848 (within one grid cell, 253 km2). The page records no territorial change between the proclamation and the Empire; the French garrison sent to Rome in 1849 is a ledger occupation, not land.

region.text: France, the Republic proclaimed after the February Revolution

ledger.note: 24 February 1848: the February Revolution overthrows the monarchy and the Second Republic is proclaimed. Infobox 'February Revolution: 24 February 1848'; 'a (second) republic was then proclaimed by Alphonse de Lamartine'.

region.text: Civitavecchia and Rome, the Roman Republic's ground

ledger.note: 25 April 1849: French troops land to crush the Roman Republic. 'On 25 April, 1849, some eight to ten thousand French troops under General Charles Oudinot landed at Civitavecchia'; 'The siege began in earnest on 1 June' and the French prevailed on 29 June.
3 July 1849: the French enter Rome. 'The French Army entered Rome on 3 July' and re-established the Holy See's temporal power; the pope did not return until April 1850.

region.text: Rome, where French soldiers 'propped up the papal administration'

ledger.note: July 1849: a French garrison stays in Rome. 'French soldiers propped up the papal administration in Rome until they were withdrawn' (the page dates the withdrawal to the Franco-Prussian War in 1870). The Papal States remain the sovereign; the region is a reading of 'Rome'.

2 December 1852 (dossier boundary only): the Republic ends and the garrison does not leave; the occupation continues under the Second French Empire, whose dossier reopens it and ends it in 1870. Recorded as an end so that this dossier pairs; the page gives no 1852 event.
2 December 1852: the Second Empire is established. Infobox 'Coup d'etat: 2 December 1851' and 'Establishment of the Second Empire: 2 December 1852'; the 20 December 1851 plebiscite ratified the coup.

wars.name: French intervention against the Roman Republic (1849)

zones.text: Civitavecchia and Rome: the French landing of 25 April, the siege from 1 June, entry on 3 July 1849

wars.outcome: The French took Rome on 3 July 1849 and restored the pope's temporal power; a French garrison propped up the papal administration until 1870.
wars.note: The page gives no 24 April date and says the pope returned only in April 1850.

certainty.note: Metropolitan frontiers unchanged through the Republic; the page records no boundary change. The Rome garrison is a point occupation, not a frontier.

notes: THIN PAGE. The French Second Republic page records no territory beyond the regime change: no area, no Algeria annexation, no colonies. Two shapes, 629,631 and 629,765 km2, differ by one cell and are both marked ok. WHAT THE SHAPE HOLDS: France plus the Antilles, Guiana, Reunion and French India (bbox -61.8..88.5 E, -21.4..51.2 N), not Algeria. The Roman expedition of 1849 is the one territorial event this page-pair explains; the occupation of Rome is paired start/end only so the validator pairs them (the end at 1852 is a dossier boundary and the Second Empire dossier continues the occupation to 1870, not a real end). Slugs: roman-republic-1849 is the counterpart name the papal-states dossier of this project already uses; no Cliopatria row exists for it (the Roman Republic of 1849 needs a dossier from the Italian group). Not covered (budget 2 pages): the June 1848 Days, the abolition of slavery of 27 April 1848 (on the page, not territorial), the 1851 coup beyond its date.
